🔥 Indescribable Compassion—or Incomplete Gospel? The Chosen’s Feel-Good Miracles Without Repentance
(The Chosen – Season 1, Episode 6: “Indescribable Compassion”)

A leper falls before Jesus.
A paralyzed man descends from the ceiling.
Crowds gasp. Friends weep.
And Jesus, with watery eyes and a gentle smile, whispers:
“I see you. I feel you. You’re healed.”

The crowd cheers.
People embrace.
Tears fall.
And we walk away thinking:
“Wow… that was beautiful.”
But was it biblical?

Because in The Chosen, the miracles are emotional, the atmosphere is cinematic,
…but the message of sin, repentance, judgment, and righteousness is either softened—or totally removed.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, aren’t these stories meant to show how much Jesus loves people?”

Absolutely.
But here’s the danger:

✔️ Love without truth is manipulation.
✔️ Healing without repentance is illusion.
✔️ Compassion without confrontation is deception.

Jesus didn’t just heal because He felt bad.
He healed because He came to break the curse of sin, not just soothe the effects of it.

📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – Matthew 9:6 (KJV):
“But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins,
(then saith he to the sick of the palsy,) Arise, take up thy bed, and go unto thine house.”
📜 Let’s break it down:
“Power to forgive” – Greek: ἐξουσίαν (exousian) = delegated divine authority
“Sins” – Greek: ἁμαρτίας (hamartias) = rebellion, guilt, offense against God

📌 The healing wasn’t the highlight—the forgiveness of sin was.
But The Chosen reverses it—emphasizing the miracle, and softening the message.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ How The Chosen strips the message of repentance from real miracles
✔️ Why compassion without confrontation is counterfeit Christianity
✔️ The real reason Jesus healed lepers and paralyzed men
✔️ What “faith” really meant in the original Greek—not just belief, but trust and surrender
✔️ Why the “healing gospel” without holiness is preparing the world for the Antichrist’s signs and wonders

THE CORE TRUTH – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE ACTUALLY SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t Jesus heal because He was moved with compassion?”

Yes, He was.
But biblical compassion is never separated from truth, holiness, and sin confrontation.

Jesus didn’t just touch bodies—He confronted souls.
He didn’t just restore lives—He rebuked sin and revealed His authority as God.

📖 MIRACLE #1 – THE LEPER (Matthew 8:1–4, Mark 1:40–45, Luke 5:12–16)
📖 Luke 5:12–13 (KJV):
“Lord, if thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
And he put forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou clean.”
📜 GREEK KEYWORDS:
"Make me clean" – Greek: καθαρίσαι (katharisai) = to purify from sin, not just disease
"Touched him" – Greek: ἥψατο (hēpsato) = to lay hold of with purpose, not a casual touch
💥 This wasn’t a miracle of emotion—it was a symbol of divine authority to cleanse what religion and law could never reach.
Leprosy in Scripture represents sin and separation:
📖 Leviticus 13:45–46 – the leper was unclean, isolated, and symbolically dead.
💣 So when Jesus touched the leper, He wasn’t just healing skin—He was declaring divine power over death, separation, and sin.
📖 Isaiah 1:6 (KJV):
“From the sole of the foot even unto the head there is no soundness in it… but wounds, and bruises, and putrifying sores…”
🔥 Jesus wasn’t just being kind—He was confronting the corruption in fallen flesh.

📖 MIRACLE #2 – THE PARALYTIC (Matthew 9:1–8, Mark 2:1–12, Luke 5:17–26)
📖 Matthew 9:2 (KJV):
“Son, be of good cheer; thy sins be forgiven thee.”
📜 GREEK ANALYSIS:
"Sins" – Greek: ἁμαρτίαι (hamartiai) = all acts of rebellion, guilt, moral failure
"Forgiven" – Greek: ἀφέωνται (apheōntai) = to send away, to cancel the debt, judicially erased
💥 Jesus forgave first—then healed.

He didn’t say, “You’ve suffered enough, here’s your breakthrough.”
He said:
“You’re a sinner. And I, as the Son of Man, have authority to cleanse you before I restore you.”
📖 Mark 2:10 (KJV):
“But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins…”
🔥 His healing was a sign of spiritual authority, not emotional reaction.

💣 WHAT THE CHOSEN DID:
❌ Showed emotional tension, silent tears, cinematic awe
❌ Reduced forgiveness to a whisper, a vibe—not a verbal declaration of divine authority
❌ Centered the scene on the healing instead of the forgiveness of sin

💥 JESUS’ COMPASSION WAS NOT SOFT—IT WAS SOVEREIGN
✔️ He forgave as King
✔️ He healed to confirm His divine claim
✔️ He always confronted sin before celebrating restoration
📖 John 5:14 (KJV):
“Behold, thou art made whole: sin no more, lest a worse thing come unto thee.”

💥 That’s the Jesus of Scripture.
Not just a healer. But a holy judge.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – MIRACLES CONFIRMED TRUTH, NEVER REPLACED IT
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t the early Church believe miracles were signs of God’s love?”
Yes—but not love without repentance, not love without truth.
They saw miracles as tools of validation, not substitutes for conviction.

📖 BIBLICAL PROOF:
📖 Hebrews 2:3–4 (KJV):
“How shall we escape, if we neglect so great salvation…
God also bearing them witness, both with signs and wonders, and with divers miracles…”

✔ “Bearing witness” – Greek: συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος (synepimartyrountos) = to co-testify alongside the spoken Gospel
✔ Meaning: Miracles confirmed the message, they weren’t the message themselves

📖 Acts 3:19 (KJV):
“Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out…”
🔥 Peter healed a lame man—but immediately pointed the crowd to repentance, not emotionalism

📖 Matthew 11:20 (KJV):
“Then began he to upbraid the cities wherein most of his mighty works were done, because they repented not.”
💣 Even in cities with the most miracles, Jesus rebuked them—not for a lack of awe, but for a lack of repentance.

🏛️ HISTORICAL CHURCH PROOF:
📜 JUSTIN MARTYR (c. 155 AD) – First Apology
“Christ’s power is not for spectacle, but for the conversion of the soul.
His healing was never for display, but to prove He is Judge of sin.”
💥 Justin rebuked Roman audiences who admired miracles but refused repentance.

📜 IRENAEUS – Against Heresies, Book II (c. 180 AD)
“Those who boast in signs but do not teach repentance follow the spirit of error.”
✔ Even in the 2nd century, the Church was already battling miracle-chasers with no commitment to truth.

📜 TERTULLIAN – On Repentance (c. 200 AD)
“Let none think that healing is enough to save; for without confession of sin, there is no entry into grace.”

🔥 The early Church never preached empathy alone.
They preached truth that led to trembling—then transformation.

💥 CONCLUSION:
✔ The Bible never presents healing as independent of sin
✔ The early Church never celebrated miracles without repentance
✔ Jesus didn’t just feel sorry for people—He confronted their brokenness, cleansed their soul, and called them to sin no more

PROPHETIC CONNECTIONS – HEALING, CLEANSING, AND COVENANT
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, were miracles and healing ever separated from repentance in the Old Testament?”

Absolutely not.
In the Old Covenant, healing always followed:

✔️ Covenant alignment
✔️ Repentance from sin
✔️ A return to the Word of God

📖 PROPHECY #1 – HEALING COMES AFTER TURNING BACK
2 Chronicles 7:14 (KJV):

“If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways;
then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land.”
📜 HEBREW KEYWORDS:
“Turn” – שׁוּב (shuv) = to repent, return, reverse course
“Heal” – רָפָא (rapha) = to restore, mend, repair spiritually or physically

🔥 No repentance = no healing
🔥 No cleansing = no restoration
🔥 No obedience = no divine intervention

📖 PROPHECY #2 – SIN BLOCKS HEALING
Isaiah 59:2 (KJV):
“But your iniquities have separated between you and your God, and your sins have hid his face from you…”
💥 Even when people cried, God didn’t move—because sin was unaddressed.

📖 PROPHECY #3 – THE MESSIAH WOULD HEAL, BUT NEVER BYPASS SIN
Isaiah 53:5 (KJV):

“But he was wounded for our transgressions, he was bruised for our iniquities…
and with his stripes we are healed.”

📜 HEBREW WORD – חֲבֻרָה (chaburah) = blows, bruises from chastisement
💣 The Messiah’s healing wasn’t emotion—it was the payment for sin’s curse.

📖 PROPHECY #4 – TRUE HEALING REQUIRES A CIRCUMCISED HEART
Jeremiah 4:4 (KJV):
“Circumcise yourselves to the Lord, and take away the foreskins of your heart…”
📌 In Hebrew thought, healing is holistic—the body follows the heart.
💥 No internal repentance = no external restoration.

💥 CONCLUSION:
✔ The prophets never separated healing from repentance
✔ Miracles were never entertainment—they were warnings
✔ True compassion from God always confronts what’s unclean
✔ The Messiah’s healing mission was inseparable from His judgment against sin

TESTIMONY – “I WAS HEALED BY FAITH… BUT NOT SAVED BY TRUTH”
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, can someone receive a miracle and still not be saved?”
🔥 Yes—and it happens more than we want to admit.
Let me tell you about Reniel, a man from Cebu who was part of a charismatic healing movement for years.

🔥 TESTIMONY:
“I was 19 when I was miraculously healed during a crusade.
I had a spinal problem that doctors said could lead to surgery.
A preacher laid hands on me, prayed loudly, and I felt fire shoot up my back.
That night, I walked pain-free. People wept. I cried. Everyone shouted, ‘God is good!’

But here’s what no one told me:
I had never repented.
I had never even opened the Bible.
I didn’t even know what sin really meant.

For 5 years, I went around testifying that “Jesus healed me”—but I was still in fornication, rebellion, and pride.
I thought the healing meant I was already right with God.
Then one day I heard a preacher say,
“If Jesus healed you but you never bowed to Him as Lord—you were touched, not transformed.”
That hit me like a sword.
I cried again. But this time—not from emotion, but from repentance.
I knelt, confessed my sin, and asked Jesus not just to heal me—but to own me.
Now I live for Him. I preach Him. I worship Him as King, not just Comforter.”
📖 CONFIRMING SCRIPTURE:

“Were there not ten cleansed? but where are the nine?
And he said unto him, Arise, go thy way: thy faith hath made thee whole.”

💥 10 were healed.
Only 1 was saved.
🔥 That’s the danger of a gospel that heals without holiness.

FINAL CHALLENGE – WHY DO YOU FOLLOW JESUS?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, isn’t it enough that I’ve seen miracles in my life? Doesn’t that mean God is with me?”

No.
A miracle is a sign, not the destination.
And signs point somewhere—or they deceive.
📖 2 Thessalonians 2:9 (KJV):
“Even him, whose coming is after the working of Satan with all power and signs and lying wonders…”

💥 Even Satan can mimic healing.
But he cannot produce repentance.

📖 MANY FOLLOWED JESUS FOR HEALING—AND STILL LEFT HIM
John 6:26 (KJV):
“Ye seek me, not because ye saw the miracles, but because ye did eat of the loaves…”
📖 John 6:66 (KJV):
“From that time many of his disciples went back, and walked no more with him.”

They loved His miracles.
They left His message.

💣 QUESTIONS THAT MUST BE ASKED:
Are you following Jesus for your pain, or for your sin to be destroyed?
Do you want freedom from suffering, or freedom from rebellion?
Do you see Jesus as a healer, or as your Master and Judge?

📖 Matthew 7:22–23 (KJV):
“Many will say to me in that day, Lord, Lord, have we not… done many wonderful works?
And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

💣 Miracles are not proof of salvation.
Obedience is.

🔥 THE FINAL LINE:
You can be healed—and still go to hell.
You can be touched—and still be lost.
You can be moved—and never be born again.
But you cannot be truly forgiven, cleansed, and owned by Jesus—and remain the same.

THE FOOL’S RESPONSE VS. THE WISE RESPONSE
📖 Proverbs 14:15 (KJV):
“The simple believeth every word: but the prudent man looketh well to his going.”

❌ THE FOOL’S RESPONSE:
“God healed me, that’s all I need.”
“I felt God’s presence, so I must be right with Him.”
“It doesn’t matter if they left out repentance—it was powerful!”
“The Chosen made me cry. That’s how I know it’s anointed.”
“Stop overthinking it. Jesus was compassionate!”

💣 The fool follows feelings, not faith.
💣 The fool loves the hand of Jesus, but not His voice.
💣 The fool is satisfied with supernatural moments—even if it means missing eternal truth.

✅ THE WISE RESPONSE:
“If there’s no repentance, it’s not the real Gospel.”
“A miracle is not my proof—obedience is.”
“I want more than healing—I want holiness.”
“I will not follow a Jesus of cinema. I follow the Jesus of the Cross.”
“If the Bible doesn’t say it, I don’t believe it—no matter how emotional it was.”
📖 Proverbs 9:10 (KJV):
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom: and the knowledge of the holy is understanding.”

🔥 The wise are not moved by crowds—they’re anchored by conviction.
🔥 The wise aren’t looking for a Jesus who fixes them—they’re bowing to the Jesus who owns them.

WHAT IF YOU DIED TONIGHT?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John… if I’ve experienced God’s presence, isn’t that enough?”
Let me ask you this:

What if tonight was your final breath?
No more reels.
No more tears.
No more healing meetings.
Just you… standing before the Righteous Judge, whose eyes are flames of fire.
📖 Revelation 1:14 (KJV):
“His eyes were as a flame of fire… and his voice as the sound of many waters.”

Not the soft-spoken Healer of The Chosen.
Not the tearful miracle worker.
But the Majestic King who judges with truth, not emotion.

📖 Hebrews 9:27 (KJV):
“And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.”
When you stand before Jesus, He won’t ask:

❌ “Did The Chosen inspire you?”
❌ “Did you cry when I healed the leper?”
❌ “Did you like how I showed compassion?”
He’ll ask:

✅ “Did you repent?”
✅ “Did you obey Me?”
✅ “Did you deny yourself, take up your cross, and follow Me?”

📖 Matthew 16:24 (KJV):
“If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.”
💥 If you died tonight:
Did you follow Jesus for comfort, or for crucifixion of your flesh?
Did you want healing, or did you submit to His holiness?
Were you saved from sickness—or were you saved from hell?

📖 Romans 10:9 (KJV):
“That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.”

SATAN’S SNEAK ATTACKS – THE DANGEROUS POWER OF EMOTIONAL HEALING
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, how can miracles be dangerous if people are getting healed?”
Because miracles without truth are the favorite tool of the Antichrist spirit.

He knows something many Christians have forgotten:
Most people don’t want repentance. They want relief.
📖 2 Thessalonians 2:9–10 (KJV):

💥 Satan can imitate power.
But he never preaches repentance.

💣 SATAN’S THREE-STAGE STRATEGY:
💀 STRATEGY #1 – CONDITION THE CHURCH TO SEEK COMFORT OVER CONVICTION
✔ “Did it make you cry?”
✔ “Did it feel powerful?”
✔ “Was it emotionally moving?”
🔥 Result: Discernment dies. People follow feelings, not the Word.

💀 STRATEGY #2 – REDEFINE COMPASSION AS AFFIRMATION
✔ Jesus is shown as “accepting” everyone
✔ Sin is never called out
✔ Healing becomes a reward for suffering, not a revelation of sovereignty
💣 The Church forgets that Jesus healed to prove He had power to forgive sin, not to validate emotions.

💀 STRATEGY #3 – PREPARE THE WORLD FOR A FALSE MESSIAH WHO HEALS, LOVES, AND NEVER OFFENDS
📖 Revelation 13:13–14 (KJV):

“And he doeth great wonders… that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men,
And deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles…”

💥 The Antichrist will work signs.
He’ll display compassion.
He’ll unite religions.
But he will never call the world to repentance.
That’s how you’ll know…
It’s not Jesus.

💥 CONCLUSION:
✔ The Chosen’s healing scenes may stir your heart
✔ But only truth can sanctify your soul
✔ Satan loves shows that showcase miracles—but silence holiness
📖 John 17:17 (KJV):
“Sanctify them through thy truth: thy word is truth.”

GOSPEL WARRIOR DECLARATION – I STAND FOR THE JESUS WHO SAVES BY TRUTH
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, I’ve been moved by Jesus’ compassion… but I want to be marked by His Lordship. What do I say?”
You say this—not softly, but with the fire of a warrior:

🛡️ GOSPEL WARRIOR DECLARATION – SPEAK THIS OUT LOUD:
“Lord Jesus, I no longer chase signs—I chase You.
I no longer follow healing—I follow holiness.
I reject every false version of You that entertains my emotions but ignores my rebellion.
I repent. I surrender. I bow.
I believe You are the Christ—not just the Healer, but the Holy One of Israel.
I will not be swayed by cinema, culture, or counterfeit compassion.
I will follow the Jesus who forgives sin, confronts darkness, and commands obedience.
I am not a fan—I am a follower.
I am not emotional—I am surrendered.
I AM A GOSPEL WARRIOR.
In the name of Jesus Christ—my Lord, my Savior, my King—AMEN.”

⚔️ NOW GO PUBLIC WITH IT:
💬 TAG 3 PEOPLE still following the Jesus of feelings instead of the Jesus of fire
📖 Reread Matthew 9, Luke 5, and Isaiah 53. Let the Spirit show you again:
Miracles follow submission—not emotion.

paragraphs:
🔥 “Matthew, Nicodemus, and the Jesus Who Waits: Exposing The Chosen’s Soft Gospel of Suggestion”
(The Chosen – Season 1, Episode 7: “Invitations”)

A tax collector pauses.
A religious scholar hesitates.
Jesus looks on… waiting. Watching. Hoping.
“You’re invited to follow Me… if you feel ready.”
That’s the tone of The Chosen – Episode 7.

Emotional.
Cinematic.
Visually stunning.

But theologically?
⚠️ Deadly soft.

Because the real Jesus didn’t invite Matthew—He commanded him.
And He didn’t gently offer Nicodemus a journey—He declared:
“You must be born again.”

There was no room for negotiation.
No time to weigh feelings.
Just a choice between surrender—or separation.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, what’s wrong with Jesus being portrayed as patient and kind when calling people to follow Him?”

Here’s the problem:
✔️ When you replace authority with invitation,
✔️ When you trade command for conversation,
✔️ When Jesus becomes someone who waits for acceptance instead of demanding obedience…

You no longer have the Jesus of the Bible.
You have a Jesus of culture.

📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – Matthew 9:9 (KJV):
“And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom:
and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.”
📜 GREEK BREAKDOWN:

“Follow me” – Greek: ἀκολούθει μοι (akolouthei moi)
→ Present imperative = a command, not a suggestion
→ Means: “Come after Me now—and don’t look back.”
“He arose” – Greek: καὶ ἀναστὰς (kai anastas) = rose up immediately, as in response to a king's call

🔥 Jesus didn’t wait.
🔥 Jesus didn’t beg.
🔥 Jesus commanded—and Matthew obeyed.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ The difference between a king’s call and a cultural invitation
✔️ Why Jesus’ words in Greek are always authoritative, never optional
✔️ The true story of Matthew’s surrender—and how The Chosen reverses the dynamic
✔️ How the show’s portrayal of Nicodemus contradicts the urgency of John 3
✔️ Why the Gospel is not a personal journey—it’s a divine summons

THE CORE TRUTH – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE ACTUALLY SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t Jesus give people time to decide? What’s the problem with making it more ‘relatable’?”
The problem is simple:

💥 When you turn Christ’s command into a conversation,
💥 You remove the very thing that made people drop everything and follow—
His divine authority.

📖 THE CALL OF MATTHEW – A KING’S COMMAND, NOT A REQUEST
📖 Matthew 9:9 (KJV):
“And as Jesus passed forth from thence, he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the receipt of custom:
and he saith unto him, Follow me. And he arose, and followed him.”
📜 GREEK WORD STUDY:

“Follow me” – ἀκολούθει μοι (akolouthei moi)
→ Present active imperative – this is a military-style command, like a general to his soldiers.
→ It’s used when immediate action is expected.
💥 Jesus wasn’t saying,

“Would you consider joining Me?”
He said,
“Get up. Now. You belong to Me.”
📖 Luke 5:28 (KJV):
“And he left all, rose up, and followed him.”
✔️ “Left all” – Greek: καταλιπών πάντα (katalipōn panta) = to abandon everything

🔥 This wasn’t emotional negotiation.
🔥 This was instant surrender.

📖 NICODEMUS – A DIVINE MANDATE, NOT A PERSONAL EXPLORATION
📖 John 3:3 (KJV):
“Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”
📜 GREEK ANALYSIS:
“Except” – Greek: ἐὰν μή (ean mē) = unless, without exception
“Be born again” – Greek: γεννηθῇ ἄνωθεν (gennēthē anōthen) = to be born from above, by the Spirit, not choice

🔥 Jesus didn’t say, “Here’s an invitation.”
He said:
“Nicodemus, unless you are transformed by God Himself—you’re out.”

📖 John 3:7 (KJV):
“Marvel not that I said unto thee, Ye must be born again.”

✔️ “Must” – Greek: δεῖ (dei) = absolute necessity, divine requirement
💣 There is no soft option. No inner journey.
It’s repentance or ruin.

💥 WHAT THE CHOSEN DID:
❌ Turned Christ’s command into a gentle offer
❌ Made Matthew hesitate emotionally before following
❌ Portrayed Nicodemus like a man struggling with trauma instead of a soul under divine judgment

💣 THE RESULT?
✔ Viewers see Jesus as approachable, but not as Lord
✔ The Gospel becomes about feeling accepted, not about dying to self
✔ Following Jesus becomes a suggestion, not a summons

📖 Luke 9:23 (KJV):
“If any man will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.”

That’s not gentle encouragement.
That’s a death sentence to self—and an immediate enlistment to His army.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – THE CALL TO FOLLOW WAS NEVER OPTIONAL
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t the early believers teach that following Jesus was about personal decision and inner struggle?”
Absolutely not.
They taught that:

✔️ The call of Christ was non-negotiable
✔️ Obedience was instant
✔️ Hesitation was the mark of spiritual death

📖 BIBLICAL PROOF:
📖 Matthew 4:19–20 (KJV):
“And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.”
✔ “Straightway” – Greek: εὐθέως (eutheōs) = immediately, without delay
🔥 No dialogue. No internal debate. Just instant surrender to the King’s voice.

📖 Luke 14:33 (KJV):
“So likewise, whosoever he be of you that forsaketh not all that he hath, he cannot be my disciple.”
💥 Forsaking all wasn’t gradual or emotional—it was expected and absolute.

📖 Acts 5:29 (KJV):
“We ought to obey God rather than men.”

✔ The early disciples weren’t “exploring faith”
✔ They were executing orders from the risen Christ

🏛️ EARLY CHURCH PROOF:
📜 POLYCARP (Disciple of John the Apostle) – Letter to the Philippians (c. 110 AD)
“Let us stand firm in the commands of our Lord, who did not ask us to consider Him, but to obey Him.”
💥 Polycarp didn’t follow a “Jesus who waits”—he followed a Jesus who reigns.

📜 IGNATIUS OF ANTIOCH – To the Romans (c. 107 AD)
“It is not enough to bear the name of Christ. We must surrender to His command and walk in death to self.”
🔥 That’s the Gospel the lions couldn’t kill.

📜 TERTULLIAN – On Baptism
“To follow Christ is not a journey—it is a surrender of will, flesh, and mind.”

✔ No warm dialogue.
✔ No inner journey arcs.
✔ Just raw, divine obedience.

💣 WHAT THE CHOSEN MISSES:
❌ Jesus doesn’t wait to be understood.
❌ He doesn’t adjust His tone to help someone decide.
❌ He speaks—and you either bow or break.

💥 CONCLUSION:
✔ The Bible reveals a Jesus who commands repentance and obedience
✔ The early Church followed a King, not a co-pilot
✔ And anyone who delayed was counted among the unfaithful

⚔ EXPOSE THE WEAK JESUS PORTRAYAL:
#TheChosenExposed
#JesusDoesNotWait
#HeCommandsNotInvites
#KingNotCounselor
#FollowMeIsACommand
#NoSoftGospel
#NotNegotiable
#JesusIsLordNotLifeCoach
#HeCallsYouBowNow
#ChristCommandsObedience

🔥 WAR AGAINST FEELING-BASED FAITH:
#EmotionalGospelKills
#RepentanceOrRebellion
#NotAFaithJourneyButASummons
#CinematicJesusIsNotBiblicalJesus
#TruthNotTears
#ConvictionNotComfort
#GospelIsNotOptional
#SubmitToChristNow
#ObeyOrPerish
#JesusDidntBeg

🛡️ GOSPEL WARRIOR UNITY:
#GospelWarrior
#IStandForTheRealJesus
#SoundDoctrineMatters
#RiseRemnant
#NoToCulturalChristianity
#KingdomOverCulture
#SolaScriptura
#TheCallIsWar
#FrontlineFaith
#RemnantRising

PROPHETIC PATTERNS – THE CALL OF GOD IS A COMMAND, NOT A CONVERSATION
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, did God always speak like that in the Old Testament? Was it always so direct?”

🔥 100% YES.
God has always called with divine authority, not emotional reasoning.
Let’s walk through His unchanging pattern:

📖 ABRAHAM – THE CALL THAT CUTS THE TIES
Genesis 12:1 (KJV):
“Now the Lord had said unto Abram, Get thee out of thy country… unto a land that I will shew thee.”
📜 HEBREW: לֶךְ־לְךָ (lek-lekha) = “Go forth for yourself” → a command form, urgent and absolute

✔ No discussion. No “Are you ready?”
✔ The only acceptable response was obedience.

📖 MOSES – THE CALL THAT SHATTERED COMFORT
Exodus 3:10 (KJV):
“Come now therefore, and I will send thee unto Pharaoh…”
📜 HEBREW: וְעַתָּה לֵךְ (v'attah lekh) = “Now go” – imperative, not suggestive

🔥 Moses argued… but God didn’t beg.
God commanded.
And Moses either obeyed—or disqualified himself from destiny.

📖 ISAIAH – THE PROPHET WHO SAID YES IMMEDIATELY
Isaiah 6:8 (KJV):
“Also I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send…? Then said I, Here am I; send me.”

💥 God wasn’t asking Isaiah’s opinion.
He was recruiting soldiers for war.

📖 JEREMIAH – CALLED FROM THE WOMB
Jeremiah 1:5–7 (KJV):

“Before I formed thee… I sanctified thee…
Say not, I am a child… thou shalt go to all that I shall send thee.”

✔ God didn’t negotiate with Jeremiah’s insecurity
✔ He declared His authority and demanded full compliance
📜 HEBREW: תֵּלֵךְ (telekh) = “You shall go” — absolute command

📖 EZEKIEL – THE WATCHMAN WHO COULDN’T HESITATE
Ezekiel 3:17 (KJV):
“Son of man, I have made thee a watchman… therefore hear the word… and give them warning from me.”

✔ The calling was clear.
✔ Delaying would equal blood on his hands (v18).

💣 CONCLUSION:
✔ The prophets weren’t invited into ministry—they were commanded into obedience
✔ Every divine call carried immediacy, gravity, and covenant weight
✔ The pattern never changed—so why does The Chosen present Jesus as if He’s hoping people will follow Him?
📖 Malachi 3:6 (KJV):
“For I am the Lord, I change not…”

💥 Jesus is the same God who spoke to Moses and Isaiah.
He doesn’t stutter.
He doesn’t wait.
He commands.

TESTIMONY – DELAYED OBEDIENCE IS DISOBEDIENCE
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, what if someone needs time to process Jesus’ call before following Him?”
Then let me introduce you to Marko, a Gospel Warrior I met in Davao City.

🔥 MARKO’S TESTIMONY:
“When I first felt God calling me, I was 21. I was deep in sexual sin, had a girlfriend living with me, and I knew in my spirit—Jesus was calling me out.
I didn’t deny Him. I believed in Him.
But I told myself:
‘Lord, let me clean my life up first. Just give me time. I’ll follow You—soon.’

I thought it was a process.
I thought Jesus would wait.

Two years later, I lost everything. My girlfriend left. My job collapsed.
I was suicidal and empty.
Then one night, in desperation, I opened the Bible to Luke 9:59–60.
Jesus said to a man,

‘Follow me.’
But he said, ‘Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.’
Jesus said… ‘Let the dead bury their dead: but go thou and preach the kingdom of God.’
It hit me like thunder:

Jesus doesn’t wait for our timing.
He doesn’t adjust His call to our chaos.
He calls. We obey—or we lose everything.
That night, I repented, got rid of every idol, and surrendered fully.
Now I preach, lead men to Christ, and warn people:

Delayed obedience is still disobedience.
The Jesus of The Chosen may wait. But the Jesus of Scripture commands.”

📖 Luke 9:62 (KJV):
“No man, having put his hand to the plough, and looking back, is fit for the kingdom of God.”

💥 That’s not a quote for artistic effect.
That’s eternal judgment from the mouth of the King.

🔥 Many are like Marko—believing but not bowing.
Admiring Jesus, but not obeying Him.

FINAL CHALLENGE – WHO IS JESUS TO YOU?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, I love Jesus and I’m thinking about following Him more seriously. Is that enough?”
💣 NO.

You don’t “think about obeying” a King.
You don’t “grow into surrender.”
You bow—or you rebel.

📖 SCRIPTURAL WARNING:
Matthew 8:21–22 (KJV):

“Lord, suffer me first to go and bury my father.
But Jesus said unto him, Follow me; and let the dead bury their dead.”

🔥 Jesus doesn’t tolerate delay.
🔥 His call is holy, urgent, and non-negotiable.

📌 THREE QUESTIONS THAT REVEAL EVERYTHING:
1️⃣ Did Jesus ask you to consider? Or command you to follow?
2️⃣ Are you waiting for your emotions to align? Or is your spirit already submitted?
3️⃣ Do you treat Jesus like a life upgrade… or a military King?

📖 Luke 14:27 (KJV):
“And whosoever doth not bear his cross, and come after me, cannot be my disciple.”

✔ No slow surrender.
✔ No partial obedience.
✔ No such thing as a convenient commitment.

💥 THE BOTTOM LINE:
Jesus is not your invitation—He is your Commander.
He is not one of many paths—He is the way, the truth, the life.
He’s not a journey—He’s a King.
📖 Acts 17:30 (KJV):
“God now commandeth all men every where to repent.”
🔥 That’s not a flyer. That’s a summons from the throne of Heaven.

THE FOOL’S RESPONSE VS. THE WISE RESPONSE
📖 Proverbs 1:7 (KJV):
“The fear of the Lord is the beginning of knowledge: but fools despise wisdom and instruction.”

❌ THE FOOL’S RESPONSE:
“I’ll follow Jesus when I’m ready.”
“I need time to process this emotionally.”
“Jesus is patient, He understands.”
“There’s no rush. It’s about the journey.”
“As long as I believe in Him, it’s fine.”

💣 The fool delays what the King demands.
💣 The fool softens what God thunders.
💣 The fool wants a Jesus who waits—but will be shocked when He returns as Judge.
📖 Luke 6:46 (KJV):
“Why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?”

✅ THE WISE RESPONSE:
“He is King—His call is not optional.”
“I obey now. I don’t need another emotional sign.”
“He doesn’t need to explain—He already owns me.”
“I follow not by feelings, but by faith.”
“Jesus doesn’t wait. I move when He speaks.”
📖 Matthew 7:24 (KJV):
“Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man…”

🔥 The wise are broken… but obedient.
🔥 The wise move now, not “someday.”
🔥 The wise don’t need a cinematic Jesus—they need the Biblical Jesus.

WHAT IF YOU DIED TONIGHT?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John… can I really be lost if I believe in Jesus but haven’t surrendered yet?”
💣 Yes.

Even demons believe.
Even Judas believed.
Even Nicodemus hesitated.
But only those who obeyed immediately were saved.

📖 Hebrews 3:15 (KJV):
“To day if ye will hear his voice, harden not your hearts…”

📌 Not tomorrow.
📌 Not after thinking about it.
📌 Today.
If tonight was your final breath…
Would Jesus meet a surrendered soldier?
Or a spiritually undecided spectator?
Would you stand before the Commander of Heaven and say:

“I was about to obey…”
Or would He say:
📖 Luke 13:27 (KJV):
“I know you not… depart from me, all ye workers of iniquity.”

💥 Feelings won’t save you.
💥 Tears won’t excuse you.
💥 Delay will destroy you.

📖 Acts 22:10 (KJV):
“And I said, What shall I do, Lord? And the Lord said unto me, Arise…”

✔ When Saul was confronted—he didn’t cry.
✔ He didn’t “go on a journey.”
✔ He got up and obeyed.

🔥 ETERNITY IS NOT A CINEMATIC MOMENT—IT’S A JUDGMENT SEAT
You won’t stand before The Chosen’s Jesus.
You’ll stand before the Alpha and Omega, whose voice melts mountains (Psalm 97:5),
…and who doesn’t wait for anyone’s schedule.

THE DEVIL'S FAVORITE LIE – “JESUS WILL WAIT FOR YOU”
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, how could Satan use something as beautiful as Jesus’ compassion to deceive people?”
Because Satan doesn’t just work through blasphemy—he works through rebranding.
And here’s how he does it:

💣 STRATEGY #1 – TURN “FOLLOW ME” INTO “IF YOU’D LIKE TO FOLLOW ME”
✔ The devil redefines commands as suggestions
✔ Christ is reduced from Lord to life coach
✔ “Obedience” becomes “processing”
✔ “Surrender” becomes “self-discovery”
📖 2 Corinthians 11:4 (KJV):
“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus… ye might well bear with him.”

💥 The Chosen gives us a Jesus who waits.
Scripture gives us a Jesus who commands.

💣 STRATEGY #2 – MAKE HESITATION LOOK HOLY

🔥 Jesus and the Children: The Chosen’s Most Beautiful Lie Yet
(The Chosen – Season 1, Episode 3: “Jesus Loves the Little Children”)

A group of children find a humble carpenter in the woods.
He jokes with them.
He plays games.
He builds toys.
He laughs at their questions and teaches them gently.

It’s emotional. It’s adorable.
It’s... wrong?

At first glance, it feels harmless—even beautiful.
But under the surface is a dangerous rebranding of the Messiah:
A Jesus who entertains more than He equips.
A Christ who connects—but never corrects.
A version of Jesus that’s safe, sweet… and spiritually sanitized.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, is it really wrong to show Jesus being tender with children? Isn’t that part of who He is?”

📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – Matthew 19:14 (KJV):
“But Jesus said, Suffer little children, and forbid them not, to come unto me: for of such is the kingdom of heaven.”

Yes—Jesus welcomed children.
Yes—He valued their childlike faith.
But nowhere in Scripture did He spend days playing with them, entertaining them, or crafting wooden toys to win their trust.

🔥 Jesus didn’t disciple kids with jokes.
🔥 He drew them with truth—and demanded faith.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ What The Chosen adds emotionally—but deletes doctrinally
✔️ Why portraying Jesus as a camp counselor lowers His divine nature
✔️ How fiction opens the door for future deception
✔️ The true scriptural model for how Jesus viewed, spoke to, and used children to teach faith
✔️ Why this episode may be the most subtle deception of all

THE CORE TRUTH – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t Jesus love children? Isn’t it okay to imagine what He might’ve been like with them?”

Yes… He loved them.
But He never lowered His glory to become a cartoon Messiah for toddlers.
There’s a difference between being gentle—and being downgraded.
Let’s break it down biblically.

📖 JESUS WELCOMED CHILDREN – BUT NEVER ENTERTAINED THEM
Matthew 18:2–3 (KJV):

“And Jesus called a little child unto him, and set him in the midst of them,
And said, Verily I say unto you, Except ye be converted, and become as little children,
ye shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven.”

🔥 Jesus used children to teach adults about conversion and humility.
He didn’t sit around whittling animals or telling jokes to win their affection.

📖 JESUS WAS FIRM—EVEN WITH YOUNG ONES
Luke 2:48–49 (KJV) – 12-year-old Jesus said:
“...wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?”

✔ Even as a child, Jesus had kingdom focus.
✔ He wasn't playful—He was purposeful.

💣 WHAT THE CHOSEN SHOWS IN EPISODE 3:
❌ A Jesus who lives in the woods, isolated, playing with children
❌ Telling stories, building toys, laughing, crafting lesson moments
❌ Soft-spoken and emotionally approachable, but never holy or feared

🚨 This is not the Jesus of Scripture.
This is a Disney-level rebrand of the Son of God.

📖 THE BIBLE WARNS ABOUT ALTERING JESUS’ IMAGE:
2 Corinthians 11:4 (KJV):
“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus… ye might well bear with him.”
Exodus 20:4 (KJV):
“Thou shalt not make unto thee any graven image…”
🔥 Recreating Jesus in our imagination—no matter how “wholesome”—violates the command to worship Him as He is, not as we wish He was.

💥 TRUTH DROP:
✔ Jesus never followed children around to gain their trust.
✔ Children were drawn to His presence because of His purity—not His personality.
✔ He never acted silly to relate to them—He spoke truth, even to their parents.
📖 Mark 10:15 (KJV):
“Whosoever shall not receive the kingdom of God as a little child, he shall not enter therein.”
💣 The power was in how they received Him, not how He acted around them.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – WHAT THE EARLY CHURCH UNDERSTOOD ABOUT JESUS & CHILDREN
📖 JESUS SPOKE TO CHILDREN—but never as one of them
Mark 10:14 (KJV):
“Suffer the little children to come unto me, and forbid them not: for of such is the kingdom of God.”

✔ Jesus welcomed children.
✔ But He didn’t run after them or tell stories to entertain them.
✔ He drew them into His divine presence, not a playpen environment.

📖 JESUS PRAISED CHILDLIKE FAITH—but never acted childish
Matthew 21:16 (KJV):
“Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise?”

🔥 The children praised Jesus in the temple.
They weren’t giggling around a campfire with Him.
They recognized His divinity and responded with pure worship.

💥 THE PROPHETIC JESUS – CHILDREN FEARED & WORSHIPED HIM
Isaiah 11:6–9 (KJV) – Messianic Prophecy:

“...and a little child shall lead them...
They shall not hurt nor destroy in all my holy mountain:
for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord…”

🔥 This prophecy speaks of a peaceful dominion, not playtime.
Children are safe in His Kingdom—not because He’s soft,
but because He’s righteous.

🏛️ EARLY CHURCH UNDERSTANDING – JESUS WAS HOLY, NOT HARMLESS

In his writings, children were taught to fear the Lord from a young age—not to see Jesus as a friend who makes wooden toys.
“We instruct our children to rise early and read the Scriptures… to obey the commandments of Jesus Christ who shall return to judge the living and the dead.”

✔ No jokes.

🔥 Early Christians taught children who Jesus was, not how to “relate” to Him emotionally.

“Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth…”

Absolutely. But let’s make one thing clear:

📖 God loved children,
But He never lowered His holiness to keep their attention.

Malachi 1:14 (KJV):
“...For I am a great King, saith the Lord of hosts, and my name is dreadful among the heathen.”
🔥 Even children in biblical times were raised to fear the Lord, not to casually hang out with Him.

📖 PROPHECY #2 – THE KNOWLEDGE OF GOD WILL COVER THE EARTH
Isaiah 11:9 (KJV):
“...for the earth shall be full of the knowledge of the Lord, as the waters cover the sea.”

✔ The goal was never to make Jesus relatable—it was to make Him known.

Isaiah 11:6 (KJV):
“...and a little child shall lead them.”

📌 This verse points to humility, purity, and trust,
Not playtime in a forest clearing.

📖 PROPHECY #4 – GOD REQUIRES FEAR FROM YOUTH
Ecclesiastes 12:1 (KJV):
“Remember now thy Creator in the days of thy youth…”

🔥 Children are called to remember, not reimagine.
They are called to fear, not to familiarize with the Divine.

💣 THE DANGER THE CHOSEN IGNORES:
When Jesus becomes a friend to children, but not their Lord,
We’ve built a Messiah in our own image.

🔥 JESUS DIDN’T COME TO FLATTER KIDS—HE CAME TO SAVE THEIR SOULS.

The danger is eternal.

paragraphs:
🔥 Fishers of Men—or Followers of Fiction? The Chosen’s Emotional Rewrite of Peter’s Calling
(The Chosen – Season 1, Episode 4: “The Rock On Which It Is Built”)

Peter is broke.
He’s lying to his wife.
He’s bargaining with Roman soldiers.
He’s on the edge—angry, desperate, dishonest.

Then Jesus shows up…
Not as the omniscient Son of God…
…but as a quiet carpenter who steps in after Peter’s life falls apart.

Emotional? Yes.
Beautiful? Sure.
Biblical? Absolutely not.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, what’s wrong with adding some dramatic backstory to make Peter more relatable?”

Answer: When you change a man’s backstory…
You change the meaning of his calling.
And when you change that…
You’ve just created another gospel.

📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – John 1:42 (KJV):
“And he brought him to Jesus. And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona:
thou shalt be called Cephas, which is by interpretation, A stone.”

🔥 The real Jesus didn’t wait for Peter’s crisis.
🔥 He saw him. He knew him. He named him prophetically.
🔥 Jesus didn’t respond to Peter’s failure—He declared Peter’s future.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ How The Chosen rewrites Peter’s story to create emotional tension
✔️ Why a reactive Jesus is a false Jesus
✔️ What Scripture actually says about Peter’s calling
✔️ How soft rewriting turns Christ’s authority into cinematic accommodation
✔️ Why this portrayal opens the door for a “follow-me-when-you’re-ready” false gospel

THE CORE TRUTH – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, wasn’t Peter just a struggling man like all of us? Isn’t it okay to show his weakness before he follows Christ?”

Yes, Peter had flaws.
But what The Chosen does is more than “show weakness.”
It alters the origin of his calling—and with it, changes the nature of the Gospel itself.
Let’s look at what really happened.

📖 JESUS DID NOT CALL PETER BASED ON CIRCUMSTANCE
John 1:42 (KJV):

“And when Jesus beheld him, he said, Thou art Simon the son of Jona:
thou shalt be called Cephas…”

🔥 Jesus didn’t wait for Simon’s life to collapse.
He called him immediately—prophetically and purposefully.

✔ No Roman entanglements.
✔ No gambling debt.
✔ No desperation.
Just a Savior with divine foresight, calling a disciple into destiny.

📖 THE FISH MIRACLE WAS NOT A RESPONSE TO EMOTION—BUT A REVELATION OF LORDSHIP
Luke 5:4–11 (KJV):

“Launch out into the deep… let down your nets for a draught.”
...And when they had this done, they inclosed a great multitude of fishes…
🔥 Peter’s response?
Luke 5:8 (KJV):
“Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.”

✔ Peter wasn’t rescued from failure—he was shattered by glory.
✔ He didn’t meet Jesus in emotional ruin—he met Him in awe and fear.
✔ The miracle wasn’t to comfort Peter—it was to expose his unworthiness and lead to surrender.

💥 WHAT THE CHOSEN DID INSTEAD:
Made Peter a schemer, working with Romans
Created artificial conflict to make Jesus’ entrance more dramatic
Delayed Peter’s surrender until his plans failed
Portrayed Jesus as a quiet fixer rather than a glorious King
🚨 This is narrative manipulation—not Gospel preaching.

📖 JESUS CALLS BY AUTHORITY, NOT BY OPPORTUNITY
Matthew 4:18–20 (KJV):

“And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.
And they straightway left their nets, and followed him.”

🔥 No pep talks.
🔥 No sympathy.
🔥 No “wait until you hit rock bottom.”
Just two words: “Follow Me.”

💣 Emotional backstory makes Jesus look like He waited for the “right moment” in Peter’s mess.
📖 Scripture shows He called Peter with no prelude—only power.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – JESUS CALLS BY POWER, NOT PLOT TWISTS
📖 JESUS KNEW HIS DISCIPLES BEFORE THEY KNEW HIM
John 1:48 (KJV):
“Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.”

✔ Jesus didn’t “wait for the right time.”
✔ He already knew their hearts, their names, their future.
✔ His call wasn’t based on emotion—it was based on eternal authority.

📖 JESUS CALLED PETER—WITHOUT SETTING UP A DRAMATIC COLLAPSE
Mark 1:16–18 (KJV):

“...he saw Simon and Andrew… and Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me…
And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.”

🔥 No argument.
🔥 No desperation.
🔥 No storytelling loophole.
They followed because the King spoke.

🏛️ HISTORICAL RECORDS – EARLY CHURCH UNDERSTANDING OF THE CALL
📜 CLEMENT OF ALEXANDRIA (c. 190 AD) – Stromata, Book III
“The Lord called the apostles, not with flatteries or emotion, but with power… the Word Himself moved them as thunder moves the mountains.”
💥 The early Church never portrayed Jesus as a quiet observer, waiting for men to crash.

📜 IRENAEUS – Against Heresies, Book III (c. 180 AD)
“It was not by persuasion but by divine authority that they forsook all and followed Him… for they recognized the voice of the Creator.”
🔥 The apostolic witness focused on the deity and command of Christ, not His relatability.

📖 CONFIRMING PROPHECY:
Isaiah 55:11 (KJV):
“So shall my word be that goeth forth out of my mouth: it shall not return unto me void…”

💣 When Jesus said “Follow Me,” it wasn’t a suggestion.
It was a divine summons—and their spirits obeyed.

💥 THE CHOSEN’S VERSION?
❌ Jesus enters during Peter’s emotional breakdown
❌ Offers hope like a friend who sees potential
❌ Delivers His call as a soft gesture, not a sovereign command
🚨 This may be beautiful on screen—but it’s doctrinally deadly.

OLD TESTAMENT PROPHECY CONNECTIONS – THE CALL WAS PLANNED, NOT SCRIPTED BY CRISIS
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, was Peter’s calling really connected to prophecy? Or was it just Jesus seeing a good man at the right time?”
🔥 Peter’s calling was not improvisation—it was divine orchestration.

The Messiah wasn’t walking around hoping to find teachable men.
He was fulfilling prophetic purpose, and Peter’s role was sealed before the world began.

📖 PROPHECY #1 – GOD CHOOSES MEN BEFORE THEY RISE
Jeremiah 1:5 (KJV):
“Before I formed thee in the belly I knew thee; and before thou camest forth out of the womb I sanctified thee…”

✔️ If God pre-appointed prophets like Jeremiah,
🔥 then surely He pre-appointed apostles like Peter.

📖 PROPHECY #2 – THE MESSIAH WOULD CALL BY SOVEREIGN VOICE
Psalm 29:4 (KJV):
“The voice of the Lord is powerful; the voice of the Lord is full of majesty.”

💣 Jesus didn’t need Peter’s emotions to line up.
His voice was enough to shatter nets and shake souls.

📖 PROPHECY #3 – THE STONE WOULD BE CHOSEN, NOT SELF-MADE
Isaiah 28:16 (KJV):
“Behold, I lay in Zion for a foundation a stone, a tried stone, a precious corner stone, a sure foundation…”

🔥 Jesus wasn’t looking for broken men to fix—He was laying a foundation.
Peter’s new name, “Cephas” (Rock), was a prophetic declaration, not a recovery project.

📖 PROPHECY #4 – THE MESSIAH WOULD BUILD WITH AUTHORITY
Isaiah 9:7 (KJV):
“...the government shall be upon his shoulder… to order it, and to establish it…”
✔ The disciples weren’t selected in weakness—they were called into destiny.

The Chosen shows Jesus “reacting” to Peter’s brokenness.
The Bible shows Jesus declaring Peter’s identity before his nets ever broke.

💥 CONCLUSION:
✔️ Jesus didn’t choose Peter because of drama.
✔️ Jesus chose Peter because of divine appointment.
✔️ The Rock wasn’t born in failure—it was called in power.

REAL-LIFE TESTIMONY – “I Thought Jesus Chose Me Because I Failed”
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, does portraying Peter as broken and desperate really change anything about the Gospel?”
Let me tell you about Marcelo, a brother from our Gospel Warrior Network in Davao, Philippines.

🔥 TESTIMONY:
“I grew up thinking God only used broken people. I believed Jesus called me because I was at my worst.
That’s what I saw in sermons, in dramas, and especially in shows like The Chosen.
When I saw Peter portrayed as dishonest, desperate, and at rock bottom—it made me feel seen… but also justified my compromise.

I started to believe:
‘I don’t need to change yet—Jesus will come for me when I hit my lowest.’
I delayed repentance. I waited for crisis.

But when I read the Gospels for myself…
I saw a Jesus who called with authority, not pity.
A Savior who said, “Follow Me”—not “I’ll wait until you fall apart.”
That changed me.

Now I don’t serve Christ because I failed—I serve Him because He called me.
And I no longer need to be broken to be usable.
I just need to be obedient.”

📖 CONFIRMING SCRIPTURE:
2 Timothy 1:9 (KJV):

“Who hath saved us, and called us with an holy calling, not according to our works,
but according to his own purpose and grace…”

🔥 Emotional gospel says: “Jesus will find you when you fall.”
🔥 Biblical gospel says: “Jesus called you before you ever stood.”

FINAL CHALLENGE – WHICH JESUS ARE YOU FOLLOWING?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, does it really matter how Jesus is portrayed—as long as people are inspired to follow Him?”
🔥 Yes. It matters eternally.

Because if the Jesus you’re following waited for your crisis,
instead of commanding your surrender,
then you’re not following the Jesus of the Bible—you’re following a Hollywood Messiah built to comfort, not convict.

📖 SCRIPTURE WARNING:
Luke 6:46 (KJV):
“And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?”
📖 Matthew 7:13–14 (KJV):
“...broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction… and many there be which go in thereat.”

💥 The Chosen presents a Jesus who patiently watches Peter drown in failure—
…but the Bible presents a Jesus who speaks with such power that nets break, knees bend, and men abandon their careers without hesitation.

⚠️ TIME TO CHOOSE:
❌ The Jesus who understands your weakness—but never demands your obedience
❌ The Jesus who “shows up when you’re ready”
❌ The Jesus who waits in the shadows of your story…
OR

✅ The Jesus who says “Follow Me” before you fall
✅ The King who speaks your calling before you understand it
✅ The real Christ who commands, convicts, and consumes

🔥 THE DECISION IS YOURS:
Keep waiting for a Jesus who enters your script

Or submit now to the One who wrote your name before time began
📖 (Ephesians 1:4)

THE FOOL’S RESPONSE VS. THE WISE RESPONSE
📖 Proverbs 12:15 (KJV):
“The way of a fool is right in his own eyes: but he that hearkeneth unto counsel is wise.”

❌ THE FOOL’S RESPONSE:
“Chill out—it’s just artistic license.”
“At least it gets people talking about Jesus.”
“It makes the Gospel more relatable.”
“You’re being too judgmental—God can use anything.”
“The drama made it more powerful!”

🔥 The fool wants emotion over exegesis,
🔥 drama over doctrine,
🔥 and a relatable Jesus over the Risen King.

✅ THE WISE RESPONSE:
“If it’s not in the Word, I won’t build my faith on it.”
“Jesus doesn’t need rewriting—He needs reverence.”
“I’ll follow the Christ who called Peter with power, not pity.”
“I don’t want a soft gospel—I want the sword of truth.”
“If entertainment distorts Jesus, I reject it.”
📖 Matthew 7:24 (KJV):
“Therefore whosoever heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them, I will liken him unto a wise man…”
🔥 The wise don’t wait for crisis—they respond to the call.

WHAT IF YOU DIED TONIGHT?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John… is it really that urgent?”
Let me ask you back:

What if tonight… was your last night?
No more episodes.
No more rewrites.
No second chances.
Just you… standing before the Jesus of Revelation—not the Jesus of The Chosen.
📖 Hebrews 9:27 (KJV):
“And as it is appointed unto men once to die, but after this the judgment.”

You will not stand before a gentle carpenter in Galilean robes.
You will stand before the One whose eyes burn like fire
—who holds the keys of death and hell
(Revelation 1:14–18).

📖 Matthew 7:21–23 (KJV):
“Not every one that saith unto me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven…
And then will I profess unto them, I never knew you: depart from me, ye that work iniquity.”

🔥 You won’t be judged by how inspired you felt.
🔥 You’ll be judged by whether you obeyed His voice when He said, “Follow Me.”

⚠️ WARNING:
✔️ The Jesus who waited on Peter’s collapse does not exist.
✔️ The Jesus who excuses compromise does not save.
✔️ The Jesus who rewrites stories for drama will never return in glory.

Only one Jesus is coming back—
The Jesus who calls, commands, convicts, and conquers.
📖 Romans 10:9 (KJV):

“That if thou shalt confess with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and shalt believe in thine heart
that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.”
💥 That’s the Gospel. Not edited. Not dramatized. Not fictionalized.

SATAN’S SNEAK ATTACKS – THE DANGER OF DRAMATIZED SALVATION
📖 2 Corinthians 11:3–4 (KJV):

“But I fear, lest by any means, as the serpent beguiled Eve through his subtilty…
For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus… ye might well bear with him.”

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, do you really believe Satan uses shows like The Chosen to prepare people for deception?”
💥 Absolutely. That’s not a conspiracy—it’s prophecy.
Satan’s greatest tool is emotional fiction that softens truth, dulls conviction, and creates a “Jesus” who fits into feelings, not Scripture.

💣 SATAN’S STRATEGY #1 – REPLACE DIVINE AUTHORITY WITH RELATIONAL EMPATHY
✔ Show Jesus relating to Peter’s struggle
✔ Show Him waiting for failure before He calls
✔ Paint Him as emotionally available—but never sovereign

🔥 Satan wants people to love a friend named Jesus
—so they’ll reject the Lord named Jesus.

💣 STRATEGY #2 – TURN REPENTANCE INTO REACTION
The Chosen frames Peter’s repentance as a reaction to rescue—not a response to revelation.
But…
📖 Romans 2:4 (KJV):
“…the goodness of God leadeth thee to repentance”
God doesn’t wait for you to break—He calls you before the storm.

💣 STRATEGY #3 – TRAIN BELIEVERS TO RELY ON NARRATIVE, NOT SCRIPTURE
Satan wants Christians to say:

❌ “That scene really touched me…”
❌ “It felt so powerful when Peter cried…”
❌ “The story was so beautiful…”
…but not:

✅ “It is written.”
✅ “The Word of God says…”
✅ “Thus saith the Lord.”
🔥 The moment emotion replaces exegesis, the Antichrist spirit has entered the church.
📖 2 Thessalonians 2:9–10 (KJV):
“…with all deceivableness of unrighteousness… because they received not the love of the truth…”
💥 Satan doesn’t need to remove Jesus—he just needs to rebrand Him.
And many are falling in love with a soft, cinematic Christ—who cannot save.

GOSPEL WARRIOR DECLARATION – STAND FOR THE JESUS WHO CALLS, COMMANDS, AND CONQUERS

“Brother John, I’m ready to follow the real Jesus—but how do I declare that boldly?”
Right here. Right now.
Speak this aloud like a soldier making covenant before the King of Glory.

🛡️ DECLARATION OF A GOSPEL WARRIOR:
“Lord Jesus, I reject the false Christ of emotional fiction.
I refuse to follow a Messiah made by movies, feelings, or fantasies.
I surrender to the Jesus of Scripture—who speaks with power, calls with authority, and reigns forever as King.
I believe You called me—not because I was broken, but because You are sovereign.
I will no longer be moved by stories—I will be anchored in the Word.
I am not waiting for a crisis—I am obeying the call.
From this day forward, I follow You with boldness, obedience, and fire.
I AM A GOSPEL WARRIOR.
In Jesus’ mighty name, AMEN!”

paragraphs:
Nicodemus, Mary, and the Sabbath: What The Chosen Gets Right Emotionally But Wrong Spiritually
(The Chosen "The Sabbath" Season 1 Episode 2)

It’s the Sabbath.
The candles are lit.
Mary, once tormented by demons, is clean and calm.
She’s preparing food. Smiling. Peaceful.
Then the knock on the door comes…
Jesus enters. No dramatic entrance. No fiery message.
Just… a smile.

Everyone is stunned.
Jesus joins the dinner. The music swells. Emotions rise.
Millions of viewers tear up.
But what if this was emotionally powerful—and yet spiritually incomplete?

What if the Jesus who enters homes…
...never confronts sin
...never declares repentance
...never reveals Himself as Lord?

That’s not Jesus of Nazareth.
That’s Jesus of Netflix.

❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, isn’t it beautiful to show Jesus eating with sinners and joining their traditions? Doesn’t that show His humility?”
📖 MAIN BIBLE VERSE – Mark 1:14–15 (KJV):

“Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand:
repent ye, and believe the gospel.”

🔥 The first words of the real Jesus weren’t emotional or poetic.
They were confrontational, authoritative, and eternally urgent.

🚨 THE TRUTH: What This Blog Will Reveal
✔️ The beautiful danger of sentimental storytelling about Jesus
✔️ Why The Chosen’s Shabbat scene is subtly misleading
✔️ How emotion replaces repentance in soft Christianity
✔️ What the real Jesus actually did when entering homes
✔️ Why Nicodemus’ portrayal lacks biblical follow-through

THE CORE TRUTH REVEALED – WHAT DOES THE BIBLE SAY?
❓ READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, didn’t Jesus sit with sinners and honor traditions like Sabbath meals? Isn’t that what The Chosen is showing?”
🔥 Let’s look at what Jesus actually did—not what feels good on screen.

📖 WHAT JESUS DID WHEN HE ENTERED HOMES:
Luke 19:5–10 (KJV) – Jesus and Zacchaeus

“Zacchaeus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house...
And Jesus said unto him, This day is salvation come to this house...
For the Son of man is come to seek and to save that which was lost.”

💥 Jesus didn’t just sit and smile. He confronted the sinner.
✔ Zacchaeus immediately repented.
✔ Jesus declared salvation over him—not comfort.

📖 WHAT JESUS PREACHED—RIGHT FROM THE START:
Mark 1:15 (KJV)
“...Repent ye, and believe the gospel.”
Luke 5:32 (KJV)
“I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
🔥 Every time Jesus entered a scene—He brought a GOSPEL MISSION, not a cinematic moment.

⚠ WHAT THE CHOSEN SHOWED INSTEAD (EPISODE 2 – “SHABBAT”):
Mary prepares for Sabbath
Friends gather for a peaceful meal
Jesus shows up at the door, says nothing profound, and just joins quietly
Emotional music plays. That’s it.

🚨 NO CALL TO REPENTANCE.
🚨 NO DECLARATION OF HIS KINGSHIP.
🚨 NO TRUTH ABOUT WHO HE IS.
Just a gentle smile and subtle presence—dangerously vague and cinematic.

🔥 BIBLICAL JESUS VS. CINEMATIC JESUS (NO TABLE FORMAT)
The real Jesus:
Preached repentance openly
Declared Himself the Son of God
Divided crowds with truth
Called out hypocrisy and false religion
Healed with power and purpose
Never tiptoed around identity or authority
The Chosen’s Jesus (Episode 2):
Says almost nothing
Enters like a guest, not a King
Avoids truth confrontation
Supports tradition without Gospel correction
Inspires emotion without biblical clarity

📖 JESUS REBUKED EMPTY TRADITION:
Mark 7:6–9 (KJV):

“This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me...
Laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men...
Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.”
🔥 Jesus didn’t romanticize Shabbat—He rebuked those who honored it without heart-change.

💭 READER QUESTION:
“But isn’t it okay to show Jesus being gentle and relational first?”

✔ Jesus was gentle…
🔥 But never at the cost of truth.
🔥 Never at the cost of His identity.
🔥 Never at the cost of confronting sin.

BIBLICAL & HISTORICAL PROOF – CONFIRMING THE TRUTH
📖 JESUS NEVER JUST "JOINED THE TABLE" WITHOUT BRINGING TRUTH
Luke 7:36–50 (KJV) – Jesus at Simon the Pharisee’s house

A woman with a sinful past washes Jesus’ feet with her tears.
The Pharisee judges her.
Jesus speaks directly, rebukes the Pharisee, honors the woman’s faith, and declares:
“Thy sins are forgiven.”
🔥 Even in quiet meals, Jesus didn't blend in—He disrupted sin, exposed hearts, and exalted truth.

📖 JESUS DIDN’T GLORIFY TRADITION—HE EXPOSED ITS SHALLOWNESS
Matthew 12:1–8 (KJV) – Jesus is confronted about His disciples breaking Sabbath tradition.
🔥 His response?
“For the Son of man is Lord even of the sabbath day.” (v. 8)
💥 Jesus declared His lordship over Shabbat, not His gentle appreciation of it.

📖 NICODEMUS’ REAL ENCOUNTER – NOT JUST INTRIGUE, BUT TRUTH
John 3:1–7 (KJV):
“Except a man be born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.”

✔ In The Chosen, Nicodemus is shown as emotionally conflicted.
✔ In the Bible, Jesus confronts him with the hard truth—you must be born again.
📖 John 3:11 (KJV):
“We speak that we do know, and testify that we have seen; and ye receive not our witness.”
🔥 Jesus didn’t let Nicodemus drift in curiosity—He dropped spiritual fire on him.

🏺 HISTORICAL & PROPHETIC SUPPORT
📜 EARLY CHURCH WRITINGS – JESUS WAS NEVER “JUST A GUEST”
Justin Martyr (c. 150 AD) – Apology 1, Chapter 14:
Describes Jesus as “more than man... a divine power who rebuked, healed, cast out, and taught with divine authority.”
✔ There is no early church record of Jesus being portrayed as merely emotional, passive, or subtly mystical.

📖 PROPHETIC EXPECTATION – MESSIAH WOULD CONFRONT & COMMAND
Isaiah 42:6–7 (KJV):
“...to open the blind eyes, to bring out the prisoners from the prison...”

✔ That’s confrontation.
✔ That’s liberation with power—not dinner table subtlety.
📖 Isaiah 53:5 (KJV):
“He was wounded for our transgressions… the chastisement of our peace was upon him…”
🔥 The Messiah was sent to carry our sin, not sit comfortably in our traditions.

💥 THE DANGER OF A PASSIVE JESUS:
📖 2 Corinthians 11:4 (KJV):
“For if he that cometh preacheth another Jesus... ye might well bear with him.”

🧠 The longer people see Jesus portrayed as passive, subtle, and silent,
the more likely they are to accept the Antichrist who will come in peace, flattery, and charisma (Daniel 11:21).

💭 READER QUESTION:
“Brother John, why does it matter if they show Jesus soft in just one episode?”

🔥 Because that “one episode” becomes the lens through which people see all of Jesus.
And that is spiritual warfare through misrepresentation.
